limits.why: 2026-10-24 Rust CI speed pass (#922, #924), measured on the runs below: job count at its measured 43; runner minutes (374.2) and longest job (19.7) about 10% above; critical path 28.1 with the harness build's cache cold on pull-request refs (about 22 once master has saved it), so 33, which still refuses parity waiting on the Rust job (38 or more); 2026-10-26 (#967, PDF ingest): longest job 25 -> 34. Rust / windows-latest measured 31.4 (median of runs 40209914303 and 40223580054): about 26 before this change (#965's run 40223499916, 26.1, and master push 40218426648, 24.2, had already passed the 19.7 the old limit rested on), plus about 4.6 for the PDF tests: provisioning the pinned PDFium library (1.2), pdfium-render compiled in each daemon override build (+1.7) and the Nextest steps (+0.8). 34 is the measured 31.4 plus about 8% 2026-11-05: startup consolidation keeps both logical parts and schema checks in one shard per OS, reducing the physical-job ceiling from 43 to 41; other limits are unchanged. 2026-11-06: one late hosted Linux-pool planner adds one brief job (0.5 min estimated) before the parity burst. The fallback ceiling stays fully hosted; enabling one measured Linux cli-startup shard removes its hosted allocation. Other limits are unchanged. 2026-11-14 (issue #1519): the report-only frozen judge probes leave the Rust job for a job of their own per OS, because a lost probe runner failed Rust / ubuntu-latest twice on 2026-11-13. Those two jobs run only on ordinary pull requests (scope full == false) and never in a batch, but this budget cannot tell, so they are counted: jobs 42 -> 44 and runner minutes 410 -> 447, exactly their estimated 19 + 18 minutes, which leaves a batch the same headroom as before. Longest job and critical path are unchanged.

parity.*: the required Parity gate reads every gated job's result

source-mutants.candidate: nightly only: its 74 jobs start only once the candidate compiles, so a broken build spends no runners on them

stress-report.stress-plan: reports only a loop that was planned

parity-pool.*: Read live runner availability only after every candidate and fixture build has finished; an earlier scope snapshot can be stale before shard dispatch.

Parity checks / ubuntu-latest / cli-star.estimate: Conservative sum of the two successful former jobs in run 41856662940 (4.38 + 7.82 minutes), before any shared-setup discount; coordinated branch proof and later two-run remeasurement pending.

Parity checks / windows-latest / cli-sta.estimate: Conservative sum of the two successful former jobs in run 41856662940 (10.37 + 12.22 minutes), before any shared-setup discount; coordinated branch proof and later two-run remeasurement pending.

Parity / Linux pool plan.estimate: One late hosted checkout plus two standard-library variable GETs, with no build or install. Estimate 0.5 min versus Scope 0.2 min in the budget; remeasure from the first two enabled master or batch runs. The routed Linux cli-startup shard measured hosted 9.70 and 11.98 min in runs 42114883218 and 42133608663; its self-hosted twins took 10.95 and 12.13 min.

Frozen judge probes (report only) / ubun.estimate: Ordinary PRs only (scope full == 'false'); never runs in a batch. The same steps' times in Rust / ubuntu-latest on ordinary-PR runs: probe step median 13.7 min (21 passes, 10.0-15.8, runs 43056784506 to 43392781569, 2026-11-11 to 2026-11-13); setup about 1.5 min (job 131777314608: checkout, Python deps, runtime 23 s, toolchain and cache 29 s); the debug candidate build 20-40 s warm there, estimated 3 min cold here.

Frozen judge probes (report only) / wind.estimate: Ordinary PRs only (scope full == 'false'); never runs in a batch. The same steps' times in Rust / windows-latest on ordinary-PR runs: probe step median 8.4 min (22 passes, 6.7-9.6, runs 43056784506 to 43392781569, 2026-11-11 to 2026-11-13); setup about 3 min (job 131776517042: checkout 18 s, Python deps, runtime 53 s, toolchain and cache 52 s); the debug candidate build 53-94 s warm there, estimated 6 min cold here.

ordinary_pr.why: Broad ordinary-PR sample: all 20 golden rows and six report-only frozen groups on both OSes; phase selections match across both runs. Batch commands and prices are unchanged; host caches and inherited master changes vary.

limits.why: 2026-11-14 (issue #1408): re-measured on master push 43456549451 and batches 43495728956 and 43476091008, each job only on runs of its current definition (guards runs instead of the four test lanes when scope skips them, so the sum overstates a run). The test job grew from 22.4 to 34.0 minutes (27.1-37.3 across those runs and batch 43525635914, whose first attempt the 35-minute pytest bound killed), so the runner-minute, longest-job and critical-path limits are about 10% above the slowest: 87.1 -> 96, 37.3 -> 41, scope -> test 37.5 -> 41. What they buy: a suite as slow as today's finishes instead of costing a batch cycle.
